title: read scans every element; write marks the end of what you keep
caption: The example keeps only the non-negative readings of a sensor log, in place. The shaded window is the kept prefix nums[0 .. write-1].

frames.text: read = 0: 4 ≥ 0, so it's kept. nums[0] = 4 and write moves to 1. The kept prefix is [4].
read = 1: −1 is negative, so it's skipped. write stays at 1, which is where the next kept value will go.
read = 2: 7 is kept. nums[1] = 7 and write = 2. read is never behind write, so you never overwrite a value you still have to read.
read = 3 and 4 are skipped (−3, −2). read = 5: 5 is kept, so nums[2] = 5 and write = 3.
read has run off the end. The answer is the prefix nums[0..2] = [4, 7, 5] with new length = write = 3. Whatever sits after write doesn't matter.
